observations.note: The track suddenly shifts into a fast, aggressive section that successfully delivers a clear peak in energy.
The sitar remains audible when the full band enters, but it has to fight against the frequency masking of the fuzzy rhythm guitars.
During the high-speed blast section, the sitar gets largely buried beneath the cymbal wash and dense guitar distortion.
The distorted rhythm guitar sounds fizzy and somewhat boxy, lacking the deep low-end punch expected in doom metal.
The drum programming and rhythm playing feel rigid and mechanical, preventing the slow riff from developing a deep, pulling groove.
The opening sitar performance sounds noticeably synthetic, with stiff note bends that betray its MIDI or sample-based origins.
The recording ends very abruptly with an unnatural cut in the middle of a trailing note.
The dark, melancholic notes of the raga scale blend quite well with the slow, plodding instrumentation to create a suitably heavy atmosphere.

overall_note: The composition offers a conceptually strong blend of a dark Indian raga with doom metal, peaking nicely during an unexpected fast section. However, the execution is hampered by stiff MIDI programming, a thin guitar tone, and an abrupt ending.
